# Envelia Studio Code of Conduct

## Purpose

Envelia Studio is committed to maintaining a professional, respectful, safe, and constructive environment for everyone who participates in the project.

This Code of Conduct establishes the standards expected in project spaces and the process used to address conduct concerns.

## Expected behavior

Participants are expected to:

- Communicate respectfully, clearly, and professionally.
- Respect different backgrounds, identities, viewpoints, and levels of experience.
- Give and receive constructive technical feedback without personal attacks.
- Focus criticism on ideas, implementations, and outcomes.
- Respect explicitly communicated boundaries.
- Take responsibility for mistakes and make reasonable efforts to repair harm.
- Protect confidential, personal, and security-sensitive information.
- Credit the work and ideas of others appropriately.
- Cooperate honestly with moderation and review processes.
- Act in the best interests of the project and its community.

## Unacceptable behavior

The following behavior is unacceptable:

- Harassment, intimidation, threats, stalking, or sustained unwanted attention.
- Discrimination or derogatory comments based on identity, background, ability, or personal characteristics.
- Sexualized language, imagery, attention, or advances.
- Insults, personal attacks, humiliation, or deliberately inflammatory communication.
- Publishing or threatening to publish private information without permission.
- Impersonation or attempts to evade moderation actions.
- Retaliation against someone who reports a concern or participates in an investigation.
- Deliberately disrupting discussions, reviews, development work, or community spaces.
- Knowingly submitting false claims, fabricated evidence, or malicious reports.
- Sharing confidential, proprietary, personal, or security-sensitive information without authorization.
- Other conduct that a reasonable person would consider unsafe, abusive, or materially harmful.

Disagreement, critical review, and good-faith technical debate are not violations when conducted respectfully and constructively.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies to:

- Repository content, issues, pull requests, reviews, comments, and discussions.
- Project-managed communication channels and collaborative spaces.
- Interactions involving project contributors, maintainers, users, or representatives.
- Public situations in which someone is officially representing Envelia Studio.
- Private project-related communication when it materially affects participant safety or the integrity of the project.

Personal disputes unrelated to the project are outside scope unless they create a credible risk within project spaces.

## Reporting

Report possible violations privately by emailing [serviciosdevsolution@gmail.com](mailto:serviciosdevsolution@gmail.com) with the subject `[Code of Conduct] Confidential report`.

Include, when available:

- A description of what occurred.
- Dates, locations, links, or affected project spaces.
- The identities of the people involved.
- Relevant screenshots, messages, logs, or other evidence.
- Any immediate safety or confidentiality concerns.
- The outcome or protective action being requested.

Provide only information necessary to evaluate the report. Do not send credentials, unrelated personal data, or illegally obtained material.

Security vulnerabilities must follow the repository security policy and must not be submitted as conduct reports.

If there is an immediate threat to physical safety, contact the appropriate local emergency service before contacting project moderation.

## Confidentiality and privacy

Reports will be handled as privately as reasonably possible.

Information may be shared only when necessary to investigate the report, protect affected people, obtain specialist or legal advice, comply with applicable law, or enforce platform rules.

The reporter's identity will not be disclosed to the reported person without permission unless disclosure is necessary for a fair process, an immediate safety concern, or a legal obligation.

Absolute confidentiality cannot be guaranteed. Relevant evidence may be retained for as long as reasonably necessary to document decisions, identify repeated behavior, or satisfy legal obligations.

Public statements will avoid identifying affected people unless they have expressly agreed or disclosure is legally required.

## Enforcement responsibility

The repository owner currently acts as the sole Community Moderator and is responsible for receiving reports, investigating available evidence, determining outcomes, and applying repository-level actions.

This single-moderator structure does not provide an independent internal review panel. This limitation will be reconsidered if additional maintainers or a formal organization are established.

If a report concerns the Community Moderator, or the reporter reasonably believes the internal channel cannot be used safely, the reporter may use GitHub's abuse-reporting and support mechanisms for conduct occurring on GitHub.

The Community Moderator may seek confidential advice from an appropriate legal, security, human-resources, or community-management professional when necessary.

## Review process

The Community Moderator will aim to:

1. Acknowledge receipt within three business days.
2. Perform an initial assessment within ten business days.
3. Identify immediate safety, confidentiality, or evidence-preservation needs.
4. Review relevant evidence and request clarification when necessary.
5. Give the reported person a reasonable opportunity to respond when doing so is safe and appropriate.
6. Determine whether this Code of Conduct was violated.
7. Communicate the outcome privately to the appropriate parties.
8. Apply and document proportionate action.

Complex reports may require additional time. Response targets are operational goals rather than guarantees.

Decisions will consider available evidence, impact, severity, repetition, power imbalance, cooperation, previous incidents, and risk to the community.

## Enforcement actions

Depending on severity and context, one or more of the following actions may be applied:

1. **Informal correction:** Private clarification of expectations for a minor or unintentional issue.
2. **Formal warning:** Written notice identifying the violation, required behavioral changes, and consequences of repetition.
3. **Temporary restriction:** Time-limited restrictions on participation, interaction, or repository access.
4. **Permanent removal:** Indefinite removal from project spaces when behavior is severe, repeated, or incompatible with community safety.
5. **Platform or legal escalation:** Referral to GitHub, a service provider, legal counsel, or relevant authorities when necessary.

Actions do not have to occur sequentially. Serious incidents may justify immediately applying a higher-level response.

The Community Moderator may also remove content, lock conversations, limit interactions, close contributions, or preserve evidence.

## Appeals

A person directly affected by an enforcement decision may request reconsideration within fourteen calendar days by replying through the same private moderation channel with the subject `[Code of Conduct Appeal]`.

An appeal should identify:

- The decision being challenged.
- A material procedural error.
- Relevant evidence that was not previously considered.
- A reason the action is materially disproportionate.

Disagreement alone is not sufficient grounds for reconsideration.

Because the project currently has one moderator, an appeal will be a documented reconsideration rather than an independent review. The final internal decision will be communicated privately.

## No retaliation and good-faith reports

Retaliation against anyone who makes a good-faith report, provides evidence, requests assistance, or participates in a review is prohibited.

A report is not considered false merely because available evidence is insufficient to establish a violation.

Reasonable mistakes, incomplete recollections, and good-faith disagreements will not be treated as malicious reporting.

## False or malicious reports

Knowingly fabricating allegations, altering evidence, impersonating another person, or using the reporting process to harass or retaliate may itself violate this Code of Conduct.

A finding of malicious reporting requires evidence of intentional misuse, not merely an unsubstantiated complaint.

## Records and transparency

The Community Moderator may maintain confidential records of reports, evidence, decisions, actions, and appeals.

Access will be limited to people who require the information for legitimate moderation, safety, legal, or administrative purposes.

The project may publish anonymized and aggregated information about enforcement activity when doing so does not create an unreasonable risk of identifying affected people.

## Relationship with other policies

This Code of Conduct supplements:

- The repository contribution guidelines.
- The repository security policy.
- GitHub's Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policies.
- Applicable laws and platform rules.

When requirements conflict, applicable law and mandatory platform rules take precedence.

Nothing in this document prevents GitHub or another service provider from independently enforcing its own policies.

## Changes to this code

Material changes to this Code of Conduct must be documented through the repository's normal review process.

The version available on the default branch is the authoritative version for current project interactions.
